paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua, son of Rabbi Akiva.
Pesachim 112a records seven instructions Rabbi Akiva gave his son Rabbi Yehoshua. In Shevuot 6, Rabbi Yose says that Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Akiva’s son, asked Rabbi Akiva a question.
And so it is in the Tosefta, beginning of Negaim.

Tosefta Ketubot, chapter 4, and Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 5:2 relate that Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Akiva married on condition that he would neither feed nor support his wife; rather, she would feed him, support him and teach him Torah (so that he could study Torah). See Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha’s entry.

notes.text: The wife is explicitly the one feeding, supporting and teaching him in the quoted arrangement. Hyman’s parenthetical explains its purpose as allowing Torah study.

Guggenheimer Ketubot 5:2 directly names Yehoshua son of Rabbi Akiva and the wife’s feeding, supporting and teaching him. It does not by itself verify the separately cited Shevuot and Tosefta locators or identify him with Yehoshua ben Korcha.
